# Component implementation and evidence record: Text editor (`tp-text-editor`)

## Delivery and source record

- Component(s) / public identity: Text editor, `tp-text-editor` (`TpTextEditor`), widget catalog kind `flattening-compound`. Companion entry `@tweakpad/ui/text-editor` (`src/foundation/text-editor/`): engine contract, headless controller and store, normalized model, tool registry, custom node API, portable content pipeline and the engine adapter factories `createTiptapEngine(modules, options)` and `createLexicalEngine(modules, options)`. No other public element tags (views are internal templates of the root).
- Requested work / claim: complete widget. One framework-agnostic editing UI (fixed toolbar, selection toolbar, slash and mention menus, link and image popovers, placeholder, read-only, shortcuts and input rules, Notion-like block gutter, drag and drop, block menu and block selection, tables with grips, menus, quick-add, ranges, merge/split, resize, sticky header, Tab rules, horizontal scroll), a declarative tool registry configured per surface, custom blocks and inline nodes, portable round trips, Shadow DOM support, minimal public API; identical look and behavior on Tiptap and Lexical.
- Scope source: user brief 2026-10-15 ("tp-text-editor: unified editor UI over swappable engines" — Core idea, UX surfaces, Block editing, Tables, Floating UI, Extensibility, Goals for v1, five reference screenshots), user answers 2026-10-15 (semantic color palette stored as names; custom blocks AND inline nodes with a trigger-character menu; image URL + optional upload hook; forms with `name` + FormData; shared portable converters; editor-wide sticky header property; reference checkouts allowed), approved plan `/Users/vanrez/.claude/plans/pasted-content-id-8cde-tp-text-editor-silly-scone.md` (copy: `tmp/component-verification/text-editor/design/approved-plan.md`).

- M0 spike results (2026-10-15/16; both engines at shadow depths 0–2): **verified**: editing through 0–2 open shadow roots with real typing, click, double-click, Enter and Shift+arrow cell ranges; a synchronous first render; capture-router pre-emption (a real Meta+B handled once by the router, Meta+I left to the engine); a fresh root per mount with clean destroy and remount; overlay geometry at Δ 0 px with 0 mutations of the engine root; engine-native cell ranges and their geometry; colors stored as names in native JSON; the clipboard hooks inside the engines' copy and cut flows; engine CSS only through `adoptStyles`; no engine UI plugins on Tiptap. **Partial**: block ids (S-28, S-29), task-item semantics (S-37), engine UI on Lexical (S-38), no foreign nodes on Lexical only with a detached announcer owner (S-27). **Disproved, fix verified**: Escape propagation on both engines (S-20, S-21). Every finding is an S-row (S-20 to S-52); the design changes are listed under "Approved-plan amendments from the M0 spike". Still open for the M4 harness from the plan's `[U]` rows: Tiptap list and quote keys, Lexical nested Enter and Tab, and the merge content order.

| DD-007 | `uwg-te-req-evt-2`, `uwg-te-req-evt-1`, `uwg-te-req-engine-7`: request outcomes are unstated: an accepted request that changes nothing (`applied` or `unchanged`); a queued `setContent` or `content.set` that a later call supersedes before ready (its promise outcome); whether the winning queued call resolves `applied` and commits at mount | V-078, V-079, V-089, C-063, C-064, C-068, C-074, C-075, C-188 and 2 more rows citing `uwg-te-req-evt-2` | Resolved in the spec (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-7`; B4b `uwg-te-req-evt-2`, `uwg-te-req-evt-4`; CRITIC §11.12, §11.13); committed in release 0.40.0 (`3db3cf0b`). Content set before ready is queued, the last call winning, and applied at mount without a change event or a commit: the winning call resolves as applied once the editor is ready, a superseded queued call settles as unchanged, and the queued call rejects with the error of the mount when the mount fails; an accepted request whose actions execute resolves as applied even when they leave the document unchanged. Final `evt-2` after the round-4 verification (CRITIC §11.13 interaction/7): a `run` that only changes the selection resolves as applied "while the editor is ready", and before ready it rejects with an InvalidStateError (`prop-2`). | gate-1 fragment report, engine 7, content 10; node source: B4b, B4a | passed |

Final `prop-2` after round 5 (CRITIC §11.13 interaction/7, §11.15 contract/11 with interaction/6): before ready, `focus` focuses the editing root "once the editor is ready and any block selection of a URL fragment (Content and formats) has applied, with the position of the last call, unless `blur` is called after it, focus moves to another element after that call or the editor is disabled when it becomes ready", and a `run` that only changes the selection rejects with an InvalidStateError. | gate-1 fragment report, engine 8, content 11; node source: B4b, B4a | passed |

## Architecture and reuse

- Component folder and responsibility boundaries: one widget folder `src/widgets/text-editor/` (element, keyboard and clipboard router, focus model, overlay geometry, announcer, tool renderers, views; no constituent tags, D2 A1) depends on one companion folder `src/foundation/text-editor/` (contract, controller and store, normalized model, actions, capabilities, tools and layouts, node definitions, ids, triggers, input rules, palette, cause tracker, strings, content pipeline, adapters), which depends only on shared Foundation owners; appearance lives in `src/presentation/families/text-editor.ts` and `src/presentation/recipes/text-editor.ts`, which bind the shared sets of R5 (in `recipes/shared/surface.ts`, G2-D4), R9, R15, R17, R24, R25 and NR-8, the shared `focusRing` and R24's divider line for the R14 separator (G2-D5) and the field boundary of `recipes/shared/text-control.ts` (G2-D23). The module table below gives each module's responsibility, owner or shared dependency, consumers and C rows; "Approved-plan amendments from gate 2 (2026-10-16)" lists the plan text that gate 2 changes.
  - Dependency rules, each with its guard: the widget imports companion modules directly and never `adapters/` (C-001, C-002); the companion imports only relative modules and at most `lit` (B3 `uwg-te-req-pkg-1`; guard `src/foundation/text-editor/index.test.ts`, C-001), never a widget module (`src/widgets/catalog.test.ts:120-122`), never component runtime code (`src/presentation/families.test.ts:75-83` admits only type imports and `export *` from `/components/`), and touches no DOM at module top level, so the pack-smoke Node run can import it (C-442, C-496); `src/index.ts`, `src/register.ts`, `src/foundation/index.ts` (whose `:45-47` re-export carousel, media and map), `src/components/index.ts` and `src/presentation/index.ts` reach neither folder (C-498: `widgetModule` at `src/widgets/catalog.test.ts:52-55` matches only `widgets/` and the two widget aggregates today, so the companion folders must be added).
  - Companion modules (the plan's Files completed from the C rows, G2-D17): core `index.ts` (curated named exports, unlike Map's `export *` at `src/foundation/map/index.ts:1-8`), `engine.ts`, `model.ts`, `actions.ts`, `capabilities.ts`, `controller.ts` (also the request detail, failed detail, outcome and surface types, G2-D18), `state.ts`; tools and nodes `tools.ts`, `builtin-tools.ts`, `layout.ts`, `nodes.ts`, `ids.ts`, `triggers.ts`, `palette.ts`, `cause.ts`, `strings.ts` and `input-rules.ts` (the shared rule table and the `AUTOLINK` matcher that C-042, C-235, C-527, C-529 and C-554 cite; D3 §3 named the module, the plan's Files lack it); content `content/{portable,html,dom,markdown,text,view}.ts` (`dom.ts`, the call-time `DOMParser` entry of C-122 and D1 §1, added to the Files); adapters `adapters/tiptap/*`, `adapters/lexical/*` and `adapters/shared/dom-geometry.ts` (added to the Files: the caret fallback to the `br` or line box, line-ordered range rectangles and block rectangles that C-539 requires identically of both adapters, written once).
  - Adapter submodules, one canonical name per responsibility (G2-D17; the C rows are normalized to these names): both adapters `index.ts` (factory, capability derivation, mount, instance wiring), `modules.ts` (structural `*Like` types, version and identity probes; `Tiptap*Like` names, never `ProseMirror*`), the action families `marks.ts`, `blocks.ts`, `inline.ts`, `content.ts` and `selection.ts` (selection actions, the block-selection classes and programmatic selections that take the anchor's format and style, S-45), `clipboard.ts` (copy and cut hooks: slice-aware on Tiptap, S-32; critical priority declining keyboard payloads on Lexical, S-33; C-131, C-133), `tables.ts`, `lists.ts`, `ids.ts`, `input-rules.ts`, `nodes.ts`, `mapping.ts`, `state.ts`, `geometry.ts` and `css.ts`; Tiptap adds `schema.ts` (own nodes and marks) and `keymap.ts`; Lexical adds `theme.ts`, `guards.ts` (critical-priority keyboard guards, the low-priority Escape neutralizer and `reservedKeys`; C-043, C-044, C-223, C-516, C-563) and `render.ts`, the only module that touches the experimental `DOMRenderExtension` and `domOverride` of the injected `html` module, as the plan's Risks and S-43 require: the task checkbox, `dir="auto"` on list items, the `tp-color` paint and the cell background (C-282, C-335, C-524, C-567). Rule installation lives in `input-rules.ts` on both engines (C-527, C-529, C-554; Lexical autolinking stays the `AutoLinkExtension` that `index.ts` configures, C-527). As built at M4 (2026-10-17): the action families are `marks.ts`, `blocks.ts`, `inline.ts`, `content.ts` and `selection.ts` with `actions.ts` and `work.ts` on Tiptap, and `marks.ts`, `blocks.ts`, `text.ts`, `selection.ts` and `actions.ts` on Lexical, over the engine-neutral core `adapters/shared/` (the action gate, the options, block, structure, fragment, text and table edits, the table planners, state and selection-state rules, clipboard fragments, code keys, content glue and geometry), which names no engine; Tiptap adds `code.ts`, and its `reservedKeys` is in `schema.ts`; Lexical adds `instance.ts`, `extension.ts`, `runtime.ts`, `document.ts`, `points.ts`, `states.ts`, `caret.ts`, `cursor.ts`, `history.ts`, `notify.ts` and `code.ts`; the Lexical clipboard writes every clipboard event in the root and runs the browser's command for a keyboard copy or cut of a block or cell selection (C-131); Lexical has no autolink extension: autolinks come from the shared matcher (C-527).

No `exportparts` (G2-D21): nested controls are themed through their own families and `setPartComposition` (B4b `uwg-te-req-pres-8`), so D2 §1.8's `text-editor-suggestion-*` names leave C-328. Family bindings add the part to every `renderRoot.querySelectorAll(selector)` match on each refresh (`src/presentation/controller.ts:234-248`) and the editing root lives in that shadow root, so a binding selector names a library host by class (`tp-button.grip`) or a widget-owned `[part~=…]` element, never a tag or a `tp-te-*` class (G2-D21).

  - Tokens and custom properties: R10's `--tp-content-<hue>` and `--tp-content-<hue>-foreground` (B2 `ccx-roles`) follow the role and foreground pairs (`docs/styling.md:18`) and the extension families `--tp-chart-*` and `--tp-syntax-*` (`src/styles.css:29-33`, `:35-51`), with hues `gray`, `brown`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink`, `red` and `default` meaning none, and join `REQUIRED_TOKEN_ROLES` through a `content` family in `TOKEN_FAMILIES` (`src/presentation/tokens.ts:4-115`; G2-D14); D2 §6.4's `--tp-palette-<hue>-text` and `-fill` are superseded. No public `--tp-text-editor-*` input exists (B4b `uwg-te-req-pres-8`); a published geometry output would follow `--tp-<component>-<measure>` (`docs/conventions.md:40-42`), and private properties are `--_tp-text-editor-*` (precedents `--_tp-emoji-picker-space` at `src/presentation/recipes/emoji-picker.ts:25`, `--_tp-markdown-flow` at `src/presentation/recipes/markdown.ts:18`). R9 takes the flow variable names from each consumer: Markdown keeps `--_tp-markdown-flow` and `--_tp-markdown-heading-flow` (`src/presentation/recipes/markdown.ts:18-19`, `:46-47`) for byte-identical output (C-467), and the editor declares `--_tp-text-editor-flow` and `-heading-flow` (G2-D21). `--tp-resize-target-fine` and `-coarse` are no theme tokens: `tp-resizable-panel-group` writes them on itself (`src/components/resizable-panel-group/group.ts:694-703`, defaults 10 and 20 px) for its handles (`src/components/resizable-panel-group/handle.ts:65-87`), so R14's owner carries them with those fallbacks for a separator outside a Group (G2-D5; C-475, D2 §3.12). Hit targets of grips and handles use `--tp-target-size-min` (`src/styles.css:103`) through `coarseTarget` and `packedExtent` (`src/presentation/recipes/shared/target.ts:6-10`); the gutter Buttons, grips, cell handle and quick-add Buttons keep Button's focus ring (`src/foundation/element.ts:74-77`; G2-D26), and the resize separator takes `focusRing` (`src/presentation/recipes/shared/handle.ts:18-21`; G2-D5).

C-393's declarations (G2-D21): `tp-te-italic` `font-style: italic`, `tp-te-underline` `text-decoration-line: underline`, `tp-te-strike` `text-decoration-line: line-through`, `.tp-te-underline.tp-te-strike` `text-decoration-line: underline line-through`, `tp-te-sub` and `tp-te-sup` restating the native `sub` and `sup` alignment, because Lexical renders underline and strike as classes on one element (`external/lexical/packages/lexical/src/nodes/LexicalTextNode.ts:202-240`) and `strong` or `em` only for its first format (`:179-187`), `code`, `mark`, `sub` and `sup` as outer tags (`:163-177`), while Tiptap nests `u`, `s`, `em`, `sub` and `sup` elements (each extension's `renderHTML`). The callout example's element carries `tp-te-callout`, which the editor's document-content styles paint with R24's callout set, and the example defines no paint of its own (G2-D13; B4b `uwg-te-req-pres-8`; C-489); vocabulary r12 now names `tp-te-table-selection` on `tp-te-table` while it holds a cell range, which closes the gap C-546 reports; the block-cursor caret rule lives in `recipes/text-editor.ts`, its only consumer (G2-D22; C-490). Open: no alignment class exists, although D1 §4.6 gave Tiptap `tp-te-align-*` because a serializer-written `style` attribute is blocked by a strict `style-src` (C-451 assumes CSSOM writes; C-398).

D2 §1.7's keys used in C-264, C-347, C-354 and C-410 are renamed (G2-D21): `bubble` becomes `selectionToolbar` (surface identity and layout key, P1-2), `blockActions` becomes `gutter` (part and layout key), `dragHandle` becomes `grip` (part `text-editor-grip`; the managed term Handle excludes drag grips), `emptyBlockPlaceholder` becomes `emptyBlockHint` (B4b `uwg-te-req-pres-5`), and D2's announcement keys gain the `announce` prefix; the labels that adapter view hooks render, and whose change remounts (C-010), are the task checkbox name alone, key `taskCheckbox`.
  - Identifiers: tool ids kebab-case (`heading-1`, `copy-block-link`) as Map actions and flow controls (`src/foundation/map/controller.ts:41-49`, `src/widgets/flow/flow.ts:342-350`); surface identities kebab-case and layout keys their camelCase forms (P1-2; the property and attribute rule of `docs/conventions.md:7-8`); dotted actions (`mark.toggle`, `table.insert-row`) and capabilities (`mark.bold`, `block.table`) have no library precedent and are the spec's (B4a `uwg-te-tab-actions`, `uwg-te-tab-engine`); node names match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/` (P2-14); presentation keys are the part names, with no `-size-*` keys since the family has no axis.

### Approved-plan amendments from the M0 spike (2026-10-16)

These change the approved plan (`tmp/component-verification/text-editor/design/approved-plan.md`). The S-rows hold the evidence and the remaining verification; gate 2 maps each change to its owner.

- **D8, Lexical color mechanism:** the stock TextNode with NodeState `tp-color`, painted by a `DOMRenderExtension` `$decorateDOM` override (experimental API isolated in one module); the TextNode replacement becomes the fallback, and cell backgrounds take the same route (S-43).
- **Escape neutralizers on both engines:** Tiptap, a first-registered plugin that claims Escape in `handleDOMEvents.keydown`; Lexical, a low-priority `KEY_ESCAPE_COMMAND` listener for a RangeSelection; the router owns Escape step 4 on both engines (S-20, S-21, S-22). This supersedes D1 §5 row 18 (`design-adapter.md:576`), the critical-priority `KEY_ESCAPE` guard of D1 §4.2 (`:446`) and the reserved Lexical `Escape` of D1 §4.8 (`:552`).
- **Ready at mount:** adapters signal ready when `mount()` completes, never from Tiptap's `onCreate` (S-24).
- **Slice-aware clipboard (Tiptap):** `transformCopied` or an adapter-owned copy and cut handler, so the payload records a text range versus blocks (S-32).
- **Lexical copy priority:** the copy and cut hook runs at CRITICAL priority and declines keyboard payloads (S-33).
- **Zero-size overlay:** the overlay box has no size and its marks overflow it, so axe contrast runs with the overlay present (S-36).
- **Adapter-rendered task checkbox:** a native checkbox from adapter view hooks, out of the tab order, named from `strings`, with a widget-owned toggle (S-37).
- **`tp-te-block-cursor`:** joins the D6 vocabulary for Lexical's block cursor and is styled by a caret rule in `recipes/text-editor.ts`, its only consumer, rather than in a shared R24 set (G2-D22); caret positions beside non-text blocks were left to M4 (S-38) and are now set by B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-9` (R3-D1, R4-D6, R5-D1 and R5-D2 below).
- **Root tabindex:** adapters own `tabindex` through `setRootAttributes()`, 0 while editable or read-only and absent while disabled (S-26), inside one adapter-owned root attribute set (S-25).
- **Paste rules off (Tiptap):** paste goes through the shared parser, so no engine paste rule runs (S-47).
- **Per-block `dir="auto"`** on both engines (S-40).
- **Block-id split rule:** a split at the start of a block inserts the empty block before it, so the id stays with the content (S-28).
- **getComposedRanges-only selection reads:** widget code reads selections through the adapter or `getComposedRanges`, never `document.getSelection()`, and hit-tests with `shadowRoots` (S-46).
- **Lexical announcers off through a detached owner** of `AriaLiveRegionExtension`, not the `disabled` flag alone (S-27); this supersedes D1 §4.2's live-region owner inside the shadow root (`design-adapter.md:435`).
- **Inclusivity parity rule:** marks and colors end-inclusive and start-exclusive, links non-inclusive, on both engines (S-44), except that the typed text follows a mark, text color or highlight set or cleared at the caret since the caret was placed (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-11`, DD-080); this supersedes D1 §4.2's Tiptap `link.autolink: true` (`design-adapter.md:426`), since autolinking runs through the shared matcher with the engines' own autolinking off.
- **Lexical block-replacing paths copy `tp-id`**, turn-into included (S-29).
- **Lexical programmatic selections carry the anchor's format and style**, as a click does (S-45).

### Approved-plan amendments from the spec-draft review (2026-10-16)

These change the approved plan (`tmp/component-verification/text-editor/design/approved-plan.md`) through decisions taken on the B1–B4 drafts: the adopted repair R26 (Q4), the request surface `content` (Q1), the planner decisions P1-1 to P2-16 and the round-4 planner decisions R3-D1 to R3-D15 whose result differs from the plan's decisions, milestones, repair rows or other plan text, the plan follow-ups recorded with R3-D1 to R3-D15 (R4, R7, R15 and the block menu while read-only), the M11 change that the resolution of DD-001 brings (`CRITIC.md` §11.12), the round-5 planner decisions R4-D1 to R4-D9, each of which changes plan text or settles behavior that the plan left open (`CRITIC.md` §11.14), and the planner decisions R5-D1 to R5-D10 on the round-5 planner items (`CRITIC.md` §11.15 and §11.16 planner items; applied in §11.17 and §11.18). `CRITIC.md` (`tmp/component-verification/text-editor/spec-drafts/`) §11 maps every decision to its draft nodes; gate 2 maps each change to its owner. Not listed, because they settle open questions without changing plan text: P2-5, P2-8, P2-13, P2-15, the other P2-16 items, Q2 and Q3, which change only draft text (Q3 settles S-27), and R3-D2, R3-D4, R3-D5, R3-D13, R3-D14 and R3-D15, which change only draft text as well (R3-D13 also has the docs name `getContent()` as the read path while the editor is not ready). The gate-2 spec items S5-1 to S5-6, which round 5 applied as well, and the gate-2 decisions behind them are left to the gate-2 merge, which records them in a subsection of its own.

- **R26, Escape on a disabled Toolbar item (Q4):** a new shared repair in `src/foundation/toolbar.ts`. `ToolbarController.#keyDown` prevents every unmodified key except Tab on a disabled but focusable item (`toolbar.ts:362` returns for any Alt, Ctrl, Meta or Shift key before the prevent at `toolbar.ts:374`, `} else if (disabled && event.key !== 'Tab') event.preventDefault();`), and the dismiss layer's document keydown listener (`src/foundation/floating-dismiss.ts:39`) returns from `#key` (`:99-113`) when the Escape is already prevented, so an enclosing Dialog stays open. R26 lets Escape pass unprevented on a disabled item; activation keys stay blocked, as `node-010070` requires. Regression scenarios: (a) a read-only `tp-text-editor` inside a Dialog, with focus on a disabled toolbar toggle whose tooltip is closed: Escape closes the Dialog (an open toolbar tooltip closes on that Escape first, R3-D6); (b) a `ToolbarController` host with a disabled focusable item inside a Dialog, such as `tests/fixtures/components/toolbar/`: the same check (the library defines no `tp-toolbar` tag); (c) flow's two toolbars, the controls bar and the node toolbar, whose disabled focusable controls (`src/widgets/flow/panels/controls.ts:653`) then let Escape pass to flow's own Escape handling, which reads no prevention (`src/widgets/flow/flow.ts:4994-5013`), checked by V-200 and V-820 (G2-D29). No draft change: B4b `uwg-te-req-key-4` already requires it. (`CRITIC.md` §11.9 Q4; proposed in §11.8 finding 8; scenario (b) and the `#keyDown` wording as corrected by R3-D12, §11.12; scenario (a) with the toolbar Tooltip closed, R3-D6 below.)
- **Request surface `content` (Q1):** a control that adapter view hooks render inside the content, such as the checkbox of a task item, reports the `surface` `content` in `tp-text-editor-request`, not `gutter`; Q1 supersedes G1 for the checkbox only, so quick-add Buttons, `items` entries, popover actions and form reset keep their G1 surfaces. The request `surface` values are now `toolbar`, `selection-toolbar`, `slash`, `turn-into`, `block-menu`, `table-row`, `table-column`, `table-cell`, `suggestion`, `gutter`, `content`, `keyboard`, `drag`, `paste` and `api` (B4b `uwg-te-req-evt-1`); `content` is a request value only, not a tool placement or a layout key. (`CRITIC.md` §11.9 Q1; §11.4 G1; §11.6 item 1; the wording of B4b `uwg-te-req-evt-1` since R3-D7, §11.12.)
- **Suggestion lists in the command list's own popup, R1 (P1-1):** the slash and mention lists are `tp-command-list` with an External input and `inline` false, in its anchored top-layer popup at a virtual anchor over the trigger character, never inside a Popover. B1's external-input profile gains this non-modal anchored presentation and B2 §18.3 the List member's Inline, Placement and Anchor rows and `uwg-te-command-req-popup`, so R1's external query owner must also keep that popup at the owner's Anchor, follow a changed Anchor without closing and treat the external input as inside for dismissal. (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P1-1; §11.7 findings 1 and 8; §11.8 finding 7.)
- **Layout keys and surface identities (P1-2):** `layout` takes the keys `toolbar`, `selectionToolbar`, `slash`, `turnInto`, `blockMenu`, `tableRow`, `tableColumn` and `tableCell`, each a list of tool groups, plus `suggestions` (default `['slash']`) and the Boolean `gutter` (default true); a tool's `surfaces` and a request's `surface` use the kebab-case identities `toolbar`, `selection-toolbar`, `slash`, `turn-into`, `block-menu`, `table-row`, `table-column` and `table-cell`. The plan's default-layouts table gains the turn-into layout and splits its row and column menus. (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P1-2.)
- **Reasons of the open lanes (P1-3):** the B.8.3 row (B4c `uwg-te-b83`) records the document lane and only the open lanes that the widget drives from its own state (link popover, image popover, table size picker, suggestion lists): `trigger-press`, `item-press`, `hotkey`, `input` and `imperative-action` open them; `escape-key`, `outside-press`, `focus-outside`, `item-press`, `input`, `keyboard`, `pointer`, `disabled` and `programmatic` close them; R3-D9 below adds further opening and closing reasons for the suggestion lists. The plan's "surface dismissal" reasons lose `close-action` (none of these surfaces has a close control), and composed Menus keep their own reason sets, with their events contained. Under G4 the image popover and the size picker are state-driven in both openings: their toolbar control is an Anchor, not a Popover Trigger, and still exposes the popup and its open state. (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P1-3; §11.4 G4; §11.6 items 2 and 3; §11.7 finding 15; §11.8 finding 9.)
- **Column resize separator (P1-4):** its value is the column width in CSS pixels, from a minimum of 48 to the larger of the scroll wrapper's visible inline size and the width the column had when a drag started or the separator received focus; the arrow key that points to the inline end widens by 8 pixels (32 with Shift, 1 with Alt) and the other narrows, mirrored when the direction of the widget is right-to-left (G2-D25, S5-6); Home sets the minimum and End the maximum; each step commits with reason `keyboard`. This extends the plan's "On the separator, ←/→ resize (Shift coarse, Alt fine)"; B1 `req-f-resizable-parts` and R14 are unchanged. (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P1-4; §11.8 finding 12.)
- **D4, selection-only actions (P2-6):** D4's "Widget-initiated actions pass one cancelable request pipeline" now covers document changes and tools that act outside the document, such as copying a block link (a request without actions that acts once accepted). Actions that change only the selection (`selection.set`, entering or extending block mode, moving between cells, revealing the block that a URL fragment names, which moves no focus) apply directly, without a request, a reason or a `tp-value-change`, and add no undo step; a `run` of them resolves as applied. (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P2-6 and P2-16 B4a(10); §10 C1 and C2; §11.7 findings 3, 6, 10 and 11; §11.8 finding 4.)
- **No preview for `json` initial content (P2-7):** initial content in `json`, which only an engine's mapper reads, is not previewed before an engine is assigned; the content part keeps its minimum block size and may change size once, when the engine is assigned or the editor becomes ready. This is the one exception to the plan's preview before ready and to its zero layout shift on late or asynchronous mounts; html, markdown and text always preview. (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P2-7.)
- **R4, Toggle sizes (P2-9):** R4 adds `xs` beside the `icon-*` sizes, so Toggle and Toggle group take the Button size set `xs; sm; default; lg; icon-xs; icon-sm; icon; icon-lg` (`src/components/button/button.ts:113`), as `req-cl-106-icons` requires once `icon-xs` exists; B2 is unchanged, and the icon-only consumers that move to icon sizes are listed under R3-D11 below. (`CRITIC.md` §8 P2-9; §11.3.)
- **Code mark and links (P2-10):** inline code excludes every other mark except a link (B4a `uwg-te-req-blocks-1`, the canonical nesting of `uwg-te-req-content-2`), so the plan's Tiptap configuration "a code mark that excludes every other mark" keeps links. (`CRITIC.md` §8 P2-10; §11.3.)
- **Block-mode paste (P2-11):** a paste over a block selection replaces the blocks with the pasted content as one `input-paste` request and one undo step, instead of the plan's "Printable keys and paste replace the blocks with an empty paragraph and continue"; a printable key still replaces them with one empty paragraph that receives it (B4b `uwg-te-req-key-6`, `uwg-te-tab-keymap-host` row 7). (`CRITIC.md` §8 P2-11; §11.3.)
- **Focus after toolbar menus and the Tab sequence, R5 (P2-12):** dismissing a menu that a fixed or selection toolbar control opened returns focus to its trigger after a keyboard opening and, after a pointer opening, to the element that had focus before the press, normally the editing root; an item that changes the document returns focus to the editing root. This narrows the plan's "Menus and popovers return focus to the editing host with its selection". The Tab sequence is the fixed toolbar, as one tab stop, and the editing root (while read-only the content's links follow the editing root, R3-D8 below); the selection toolbar, the gutter and the table controls are reached through Alt+F10, and Escape, Tab or Shift+Tab in the selection toolbar or the gutter return to the editing root. B1's contextual profile now allows a Toolbar kept out of the Tab sequence, so `ToolbarController` gains that option, which the R5 owner and the gutter use (G2-D2). Escape on the fixed toolbar with no menu or tooltip open is neither consumed nor prevented (R26), and an open toolbar tooltip closes on that Escape first (R3-D6 below). (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P2-12; §11.7 findings 13 and 14; §11.8 findings 2 and 8.)
- **D9, node names (P2-14):** a custom node name matches `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/` and is none of `doc`, `root`, `text`, `hard-break`, `paragraph`, `heading`, `quote`, `code`, `list`, `list-item`, `list-bullet`, `list-ordered`, `list-task`, `task`, `divider`, `image`, `table`, `table-row`, `table-cell`, `table-header` and `cursor` (added in round 1 for `tp-te-block-cursor`), nor a built-in tool identifier; the plan's "reserved node names" unit tests check this list. (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P2-14; §11.7 finding 4.)
- **M11, content an engine cannot represent (P2-16, B4a(5)):** whether loaded or carried over by an engine swap, it is converted, never dropped: each such block becomes a paragraph holding its text as the text format writes it, a line break becoming a hard break, and each such inline node becomes its text, or nothing when it has none, with one diagnostic naming the converted kinds. M11's "engine swap with a dropped-node diagnostic" therefore checks that conversion and its diagnostic; the spec fixes no code literal, and gate 2 names the diagnostic `text-editor-content-converted` in place of the planner's `text-editor-content-dropped`, which misnames a conversion (G2-D21). (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P2-16; §11.4 G2.)
- **Redo chord (P2-16, B4b(9)):** Ctrl+Y redoes only outside Apple platforms, so the plan's "Mod+Z / Mod+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y" row becomes Mod+Z; Mod+Shift+Z, and Ctrl+Y outside Apple platforms (B4a `uwg-te-tab-tools` row 1, B4b `uwg-te-tab-keymap` row 1). It also supersedes the platform-free `Mod+y` and `Ctrl+y` reservations of D1 §4.8 (`design-adapter.md:551-552`): on Apple platforms a reserved `Mod+y` is consumed without effect (C-043). (`CRITIC.md` §11.3 P2-16.)
- **M11, a move into another document (DD-001):** a DOM move keeps the engine instance only within one document; a reconnection into another document before the release destroys the instance and mounts anew with its content carried over through portable HTML, as replacing the engine does, and that remount moves no focus by itself. M11's "reconnection (`updateRoot` / `setRootElement`)" therefore becomes a check of that remount, with no root refresh inside the adapters (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-8`; B3 `uwg-te-req-render-2`, `uwg-t-195`). (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 DD-001 and follow-ups; §11.13 interaction/11.)
- **Caret beside blocks that are not textblocks (R3-D1):** an adapter never leaves the selection beside a block that is not a textblock: a key that would place it there keeps it in the nearest textblock or cell in that direction, or leaves it unchanged when there is none, so that `tp-te-block-cursor` marks only a transient engine caret (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-9`). This decides the caret positions that the M0 amendment on `tp-te-block-cursor` left to M4, where the parity harness now verifies them; R4-D6 below replaces its sentence and settles presses beside such blocks and ArrowLeft or ArrowRight from a block-selected atom (`CRITIC.md` §11.14). (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 R3-D1.)
- **Block identifiers at a split and a join (R3-D3):** Enter at the start of a non-empty block other than a code block creates an empty paragraph, or an empty list item in a list, before it with a fresh identifier, so that the block keeps its identifier with its content; when two blocks join, the one that holds the first character of the joined content keeps its identifier. This refines the M0 amendment "Block-id split rule" (B4a `uwg-te-req-content-7`; B4b `uwg-te-lis-up` i2). (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 R3-D3.)
- **Escape with a toolbar Tooltip open (R3-D6):** on a fixed-toolbar control with no menu or tooltip open, Escape is neither consumed nor prevented, and an open tooltip of the toolbar closes on that Escape first, as Tooltip behavior provides (B4b `uwg-te-req-key-4`, `uwg-te-tab-keymap-host` r3), so R26's scenario (a) asserts with the toolbar Tooltip closed, or expects two Escapes. (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 R3-D6 and follow-ups.)
- **Read-only links in the Tab sequence (R3-D8, narrows P2-12(a)):** the Tab sequence stays the fixed toolbar, as one tab stop, and the editing root, except that while the editor is read-only the links of the content stay in the sequential focus order after the editing root, so that keyboard users follow them natively (B4b `uwg-te-req-a11y-2`). The round-4 verification aligned the keys: while read-only, Tab and Shift+Tab in a table cell are not consumed, and Tab first reaches those links (B4a `uwg-te-req-tables-7`; B4b `uwg-te-req-key-3`, `uwg-te-tab-keymap-host` r8; `CRITIC.md` §11.13 interaction/2). (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 R3-D8.)
- **More reasons for the open lanes (R3-D9):** a suggestion list also opens when a key, a press, a paste, a drop or an undo puts the caret after a trigger that was not dismissed, and closes when an edit of any cause, a key or a press leaves its trigger context, so that P1-3's opening reasons gain `input-paste`, `keyboard`, `pointer`, `drag` and `engine` and its closing reasons `input-paste`, `hotkey`, `drag`, `engine` and `imperative-action`; every one of them is in the B4c reason set, which is unchanged (B4b `uwg-te-par-evt-1`, `uwg-te-tab-reasons` r12 and r13; B4c `uwg-te-b83`). (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 R3-D9.)
- **Block menu chord on layouts that type `/` with Shift and a digit (R3-D10):** Mod+/ opens the block menu unless a binding with more modifiers matches the same keystroke. On layouts that type `/` with Shift and a digit key, the keystroke also matches Mod+Shift with that digit, which wins under the Foundation key-binding priority (where `/` is Shift+7, Mod+Shift+7 toggles the ordered list), so that the block menu has no key chord from text there and opens from the gutter grip, which Alt+F10 reaches; Shift+F10 and the context menu key still open it in block mode or on a focused grip. Both chords and the Foundation stay unchanged (B4a `uwg-te-req-blocks-3`, `uwg-te-tab-tools-actions` r5 c3; B4b `uwg-te-tab-keymap` r14). With DD-064 and the round-4 verification, Mod+/ targets the block selection, or else the blocks that the caret, the text selection or the cell range touches, where the plan names the caret block only (`CRITIC.md` §11.13 interaction/6). (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 R3-D10.)
- **R4 regressions (R3-D11):** R4's regression list adds three icon-only Toggle consumers that move to icon sizes, as B2 requires (committed in release 0.38.0, `b08e78ec`): the Theme switcher group variant (`src/components/theme-switcher/theme-switcher.ts:283-301`, `size=${state.size}`, which must take `icon-sm` or `icon`), the Easing editor presets toggle (`src/widgets/easing-editor/easing-editor.ts:1468-1479`, `size="sm"`) and Flow's control toggles (`src/widgets/flow/panels/controls.ts:671-743`, at the default size). The fired B2 review `ucl16-theme-switcher-dep-3` was approved before the B2 content commit (`be79196e`, 0.37.1), which left the Theme switcher section unchanged, so its summary names no icon size for the group variant. (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 R3-D11; §11.10 F6.)
- **R7, AltGraph rule (round-3 follow-up):** R7 and D7 narrow "never match Mod chords under AltGraph" to no Mod chord without Alt while AltGraph is active, as B1 `flx-0139` ("never match a Mod chord without Alt while AltGraph is active") and B4b `uwg-te-req-key-2` state, because Firefox reports AltGraph for Option on macOS and for Ctrl+Alt on Windows; R7's unit tests add the Firefox Option and Ctrl+Alt cases. (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 follow-ups; §11.10 F1.)
- **R15, flow marquee fill (round-3 follow-up):** R15's flow marquee regression records a visible change: the marquee fill moves from `primary` (`src/presentation/recipes/flow.ts:15`) to the `accent` fill of the shared selection recipe, as B2 `uwg-te-sel-req-overlay` requires for filled selection areas (C-476, V-220). (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 follow-ups; §11.10 F7.)
- **No block menu at a virtual anchor in v1 (round-3 follow-up):** a block menu opened at a virtual anchor, which would let a read-only editor copy a block link from that menu, is out of v1, because CL Menu has no Anchor property and it would add public API; while the editor is read-only or disabled the block menu does not open (B4a `uwg-te-req-blocks-3`). (`CRITIC.md` §11.12 follow-ups; §11.10 C17 and item 13.)
- **Exclusive toolbar toggles (R4-D1, DD-041):** wherever the layout of the fixed or the selection toolbar lists both tools of an exclusive pair, `blockquote` with `code-block` or `superscript` with `subscript`, the two render together as one Toggle group (`tp-toggle-group`) with single selection at the place of the one that the layout lists first, so that pressing the pressed item releases it, back to a paragraph or to neither mark (`toggleSelection` returns `[]` in single mode, `src/components/toggle-group/selection.ts:20-26`); a toolbar layout that lists only one of a pair renders it as a Toggle, and the More menu of the fixed toolbar, like the menu of the `more` tool, keeps the two as checkbox items. The plan's default fixed toolbar therefore renders blockquote with code-block and superscript with subscript as two such groups, whose items join the toolbar's roving order (R3; B2 `uwg-te-toggle-group-req-toolbar`), while tool identifiers, kinds, layout keys and the default layouts stay as planned and CL `ucl16-toggle-q3` holds without a B2 change (B4a `uwg-te-req-tools-1`). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D1, deciding §11.12 planner item 1.)
- **Status part (R4-D2, DD-078):** the plan's part list gains `text-editor-status`, the status region over the content while the editor is not ready, which holds a polite status with a Spinner and the loading text while the engine loads, or an alert with the error text while the status is error, and takes the presentation of the Status of Map from one shared recipe (the shared status set NR-8; precedent `map-status`); the drag preview and the guide line of a column resize stay without a part, as the plan's part list has them, the drag preview taking the document content profile. The part has an anatomy table of its own because `uwg-te-tab-anatomy` is at the size cap (B4b `uwg-te-tab-anatomy-status`, `uwg-te-par-ana-1`, `uwg-te-req-pres-1`, `uwg-te-req-pres-2`). R5-D3 below limits the region to the loading and error statuses (`CRITIC.md` §11.15 planner item 3). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D2, deciding §11.12 planner item 2.)
- **Mod+A (R4-D3, DD-095):** Mod+A stays engine-owned and is never reserved (D7), and it selects the whole document on every engine, from any position, a table cell or a code block included; the state reports that selection as text from the first to the last text point of the document while the engine keeps its own whole-document selection, so that copy, cut, typing and deletion act on the whole document, and Escape from it selects every top-level block, as step 5 of the plan's Escape order enters block mode (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-4`, `uwg-te-req-blocks-4`). This supersedes D1 §5 row 20, under which a first press selects the block's text and a second block-selects all top-level blocks. R5-D6, R5-D7 and R5-D2 below settle Mod+A while the editor is read-only, what deleting, cutting, typing or pasting over that selection leaves and what its copy records, and `engine-9` in a document that starts with an atom (`CRITIC.md` §11.15 planner items 6, 7 and 2). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D3, deciding §11.12 planner item 3.)
- **Code-block Backspace and ArrowUp exit (R4-D4, DD-095):** Backspace with a collapsed caret at the start of a code block turns it into a paragraph, its line breaks becoming hard breaks, as at the start of a heading or quote, and only a further Backspace acts as at the start of a paragraph, where Tiptap would join the code block into the block before it; ArrowUp at the start of a code block that no block precedes inserts a paragraph before it and moves the caret into it, mirroring the ArrowDown exit, as Tiptap's default `exitOnArrowUp` does (`external/tiptap/packages/extension-code-block/src/code-block.ts:371-395`) and the Lexical adapter adds, since it is the only keyboard path to a paragraph above a leading code block. The plan's parity rules gain both, and D1 §5 row 38, the exit by triple Enter or ArrowDown only, is superseded (B4a `uwg-te-req-parity-1`). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D4, deciding §11.12 planner item 4.)
- **Insert Button without the slash suggestion (R4-D5, DD-065):** the plan's gutter "+", which inserts below (Alt: above) and opens slash, does so while the `suggestions` layout key lists `slash`; when it does not, the insert Button inserts the same new block without the trigger, in one request with reason `trigger-press`, or makes no request when the block is an empty paragraph or an empty list item, and then places the caret in that block with focus in the editing root. The round-5 verification makes the insert Button the named exception to keyboard activation keeping focus on a control that opens no surface, where the plan says "Keyboard activation in the toolbars keeps focus there" (B4a `uwg-te-req-blocks-2`; B4b `uwg-te-tab-anatomy` r8 c1, `uwg-te-req-a11y-2`). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D5, deciding §11.12 planner item 5; §11.15 contract/12.)
- **Selection beside blocks that are not textblocks (R4-D6, DD-095):** replacing R3-D1's sentence, an adapter never leaves the selection beside a block that is not a textblock: a key that would place it there selects the adjacent block in that direction when the selection is a block selection of an atom and that block is an atom block, and otherwise moves it into the nearest textblock or cell in that direction, at its start when moving forward and at its end when moving backward, or leaves it unchanged when there is none; a press that the engine resolves there moves the selection head, and without Shift the anchor as well, to the text point nearest to the press point, so that `tp-te-block-cursor` marks only a transient engine caret (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-9`). This settles the presses beside such blocks and the engines' ArrowLeft and ArrowRight from a selected atom, which `key-6` leaves unbound and the M0 amendment on `tp-te-block-cursor` left to M4; the Lexical adapter normalizes its presses beside such blocks and its exits from a selected atom. R5-D1 and R5-D2 below amend its rule, settling the atom branch from a caret or from a block selection of a block that is not an atom and the rule against Mod+A in a document that starts with an atom (`CRITIC.md` §11.15 planner items 1 and 2). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D6, deciding §11.13 planner item 1; §11.15 interaction/3.)
- **Suggestion tools off surfaces, color channels and valueless runs (R4-D7):** a suggestion tool takes no place on a surface: `*` does not expand to it, its identifier in the layout of a surface is skipped with a diagnostic, as an unknown identifier is, and a suggestion list opens only from its trigger in the content, the slash menu also from the insert Button of the gutter, which refines the plan's resolution rules ("`'*'` expands to the remaining tools for that surface", "Unknown ids raise diagnostics"). `channel` takes the color channels `text`, `highlight` and `background`, a color tool with several channels takes `{ channel, color }` with one of the channels it offers and a palette name or `default`, and a color, radio-menu, menu or suggestion tool run without a value settles as unchanged, while a link, image or table-size tool run without a value opens its surface (B4a `uwg-te-par-tools-1`, `uwg-te-req-tools-1`, `uwg-te-req-tools-4`; B4b `uwg-te-tab-reasons` r12 c0, `uwg-te-req-evt-5`). R5-D5 below settles what `run` does with a value outside the domain of its kind (`CRITIC.md` §11.15 planner item 5). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D7, deciding §11.13 planner item 2; §11.15 contract/13.)
- **Positions in a table touch the table (R4-D8):** a caret, a text selection or a cell range inside a table touches the table, never a paragraph of a cell, so that Escape in a table, after a cell range has collapsed to a caret (steps 4 and 5 of the plan's Escape order), selects the table, and Mod+/, Mod+D and Mod+Shift+Up or Down, which act on the blocks that the selection touches as Escape selects them, open the block menu for the table, duplicate it or move it, where the plan names the caret block for Mod+/ (B4a `uwg-te-req-blocks-4`, and through it `uwg-te-req-blocks-3`, `uwg-te-req-blocks-5` and B4b `uwg-te-tab-keymap` r11, r12 and r14). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D8, from §11.13 "Noticed, not changed".)
- **Up and Down through atoms in block mode (R4-D9):** the plan's block-mode "↑/↓ select the previous or next block" holds except from a block selection that holds only one atom block, where Up and Down without Shift select the adjacent block when it is an atom block, and otherwise place the caret at the end of the nearest textblock or cell before it (Up) or at the start of the nearest one after it (Down), which ends block mode, or leave the selection unchanged when there is none; Shift+Up and Shift+Down extend as before. An arrow key onto an atom, which enters block mode on it (B4a `uwg-te-req-blocks-4`), therefore never leads on to a block selection of the next paragraph, which a printable key would replace (B4b `uwg-te-req-key-6`, `uwg-te-tab-keymap-host` r4). R5-D8 below settles ArrowLeft and ArrowRight from other block selections (`CRITIC.md` §11.15 planner item 8). (`CRITIC.md` §11.14 R4-D9, from §11.13 "Noticed, not changed".)
- **Atom branch from every start (R5-D1, DD-095):** in the R4-D6 line above, "when the selection is a block selection of an atom and that block is an atom block" becomes "when that block is an atom block", so that an arrow key that would leave the selection beside an atom block selects that atom, and block mode starts on it, from a caret, a text selection, a cell at a table edge or a block selection alike, which the Lexical adapter normalizes for its table exits and `$exitNodeSelectionToward` (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-9`; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.15 planner item 1); the sentence of `uwg-te-req-tables-7` on the arrow keys at a table's edges was DD-106, which SC-D4 settles in 0.40.1 (`edd84f2a`).
- **Only a collapsed selection is kept off non-textblocks (R5-D2, DD-095):** in the R4-D6 line above, "an adapter never leaves the selection beside a block that is not a textblock" now concerns a collapsed selection, so that the whole-document selection of Mod+A keeps a leading atom block on every engine and a press with Shift still moves only the selection head (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-9`; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.15 planner item 2).
- **No status region while idle (R5-D3, DD-078):** the approved plan's States row "**loading, idle, error:** status region; controls `aria-disabled`" becomes a status region only while the engine loads or the status is error, and with it the R4-D2 line's "status region over the content while the editor is not ready", so that while idle the controls keep their disabled semantics, the missing engine is reported by the "no engine assigned" diagnostic of `uwg-te-req-evt-5` (planned code `text-editor-engine-missing`, C-083) and the pre-engine preview of `uwg-te-req-pres-5` stays visible (B4b `uwg-te-tab-anatomy-status` r1, `uwg-te-tab-anatomy` r1 c1; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.15 planner item 3).
- **Item descriptions for assistive technology (R5-D4, B2 part):** the description that a slash or mention entry shows (a tool's `description?` in the plan's tool shape, or the description of a suggestion item) is the accessible description of its Command palette Item and leaves the Item's accessible name its label, which the plan's "Slash and mention" row and its accessibility snapshots leave unstated (B2 `uwg-te-command-req-description`); the plan's "otherwise LiveAnnouncer speaks the item" is R5-D4's B4b part (`uwg-te-req-a11y-3`), whose line follows. (`CRITIC.md` §11.15 planner item 4, contract/7 with interaction/8; §11.17.)
- **Description in the suggestion announcement (R5-D4, B4b part):** the LiveAnnouncer of the plan's Slash and mention row ("otherwise LiveAnnouncer speaks the item") now speaks each newly highlighted item with its label, its description when it has one, and its position among the items, the description being the Item's accessible description and the label its accessible name under the B2 part of R5-D4 (B4b `uwg-te-req-a11y-3`; B2 `uwg-te-command-req-description`; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.15 planner item 4 with §11.17).
- **`run` values outside their domain (R5-D5):** the plan's `run(toolId | action | actions, {value?, sourceEvent?})` now rejects a value outside the domain of its tool's kind before any request is dispatched, with a RangeError for rows or columns that are not integers within the ranges of the table size picker and with a TypeError for any other such value, ahead of the NotSupportedError cases of the request pipeline, which settles what the R4-D7 line left open (B4a `uwg-te-req-tools-4`; B4b `uwg-te-req-evt-1`; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.15 planner item 5); the domain of the kinds that take no value and the request detail of such a rejection were DD-111 and DD-113, which SC-D1 and SC-D2 settle in 0.40.1 (`edd84f2a`).
- **Mod+A while read-only (R5-D6):** the plan's "**Engine-owned:** … Mod+A" (Keyboard) and the R4-D3 line now hold while the editor is editable, while a read-only editor binds Mod+A in the editing root under the editing-host profile to select the content of the editing root and nothing outside it, whose copy writes that content in the portable profile, D7's "`Mod+A` and `Escape` are never reserved" still holding for adapters, with an M4 check that each engine's copy follows the DOM selection that this binding sets (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-4`, `uwg-te-req-engine-11`; B4b `uwg-te-req-key-3`, `uwg-te-tab-keymap-host` r13; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.15 planner item 6); what `state` reports for that selection, what its copy records and whether Escape from it selects every top-level block were DD-110, which SC-D5 settles in 0.40.1 (`edd84f2a`), and the profile's "editable element" is DD-107.
- **After the Mod+A selection (R5-D7, DD-095):** the R4-D3 line's whole-document selection, on which "copy, cut, typing and deletion act", now leaves one empty paragraph with a fresh identifier when it is deleted or cut, takes typing and a paste as at the caret in that paragraph and is copied as a text range, as on the block-mode path where deleting every block leaves such a paragraph, which the Lexical adapter normalizes (B4a `uwg-te-req-engine-4`; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.15 planner item 7).
- **Left and Right in block mode (R5-D8):** the plan's Block mode row "↑/↓ select the previous or next block. Shift+↑/↓ extend." gains ←/→ without Shift, which from any block selection act before the first selected block (the arrow key that points to the inline start in the direction of the widget) or after the last (the other) and select the adjacent atom block or else place the caret at the end of the nearest textblock or cell before or at the start of the nearest one after, ending block mode, so that the engines' ArrowLeft and ArrowRight from a selected atom, which the R4-D6 line leaves to `engine-9`, become widget bindings with the same targets (B4b `uwg-te-req-key-6`, `uwg-te-tab-keymap-host` r14; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.15 planner item 8).
- **Point of insertion of a selection that is not a caret (R5-D9, DD-044, DD-050):** the plan's Image popover row "The image is inserted at the remembered range" now inserts at the point of insertion of the remembered selection, which for a block that a tool inserts is the end of a text selection in document order, the place after the last block of a block selection and, with no selection, the end of the document, where the image popover and the table size picker then also open (B4a `uwg-te-req-blocks-1`, `uwg-te-req-surfaces-4`, `uwg-te-req-tables-2`; `CRITIC.md` §11.18, deciding §11.16 planner item 1); the point of insertion of a cell range is DD-112.
- **Command list Matching row (R5-D10):** B2 §18.3 gains the Matching row of the List member (`uwg-te-command-props-matching`: contains, fuzzy, prefix or exact, default contains, with source, searchDelay, highlightMatches (default false) and matchFields as in the Matching of Select), which documents the existing `tp-command-list` API that the plan's "Slash and mention" row ("Mention `source` is async, with abort and `busy`") and G2-D19 rely on, so that the Command list docs (C-259) list it beside Inline, Placement, Anchor and External input; the row changes no planned behavior, and the scope of CL `ucl18-command-ranking` and of the Filter row against the List member used alone are DD-108 and DD-109. (`CRITIC.md` §11.16 planner item 2; §11.17.)

### Approved-plan amendments from gate 2 (2026-10-16)

These change the approved plan (`tmp/component-verification/text-editor/design/approved-plan.md`) through the gate-2 owner decisions G2-D1 to G2-D30 (`tmp/component-verification/text-editor/gate2/G2-DECISIONS.md`, with the merge resolutions in `gate2/RESOLUTIONS.md`), which answer the open questions of the gate-2 survey (`gate2/repairs/repairs.md`, `gate2/amendments/amendments.md`, `gate2/modules/modules.md`, `gate2/composition/composition.md`), and through the new shared repairs NR-1 to NR-8 that they adopt, with the capability rows C-576 to C-583 and the regression scenarios V-835 to V-842; where a later decision changed one (R4-D2 merged G2-D12, S5-4 amended G2-D23), the line gives the result. The decisions that needed a draft change were applied in round 5 as the gate-2 spec items S5-1 to S5-6 (`CRITIC.md` §11.14, with the fixes of §11.15 and §11.16), and their lines name the nodes that carry them, committed in release 0.38.0 (`b08e78ec`) for S5-1 (B2) and in release 0.40.0 (`3db3cf0b`) for S5-2 to S5-6 (B4); the R3-D and R4-D decisions stay in the subsection above, and the module table below maps each change to its module.

- **NR-1, deferred release and mount session (G2-D8):** a new row of the plan's Shared repairs table. `deferRelease(view, release)` beside `Scheduler` (`src/foundation/services.ts:72-133`) and one engine-session owner (supersession through an `AbortController`, the `live()` guard, ready once, a superseded instance destroyed on arrival, fail and teardown) replace the two-frame deferred release of Map (`src/foundation/map/controller.ts:237-252`) and of the media player (`deferMediaDestroy`, `src/foundation/media/store.ts:692-700`, used at `src/components/media-player/player.ts:44`, `:546`) and Map's mount session (`src/foundation/map/controller.ts:217-403`), so the controller's "deferred destroy" of the plan's Layers and M11 is that shared owner, which `MapController`, the media player and the editor use. The public `deferMediaDestroy` (`@tweakpad/ui`, `@tweakpad/ui/media`) is removed directly, with no alias or deprecation, and a changeset records it. C-576 and V-835, with the existing regressions `src/foundation/map/controller.test.ts:49-59` and `src/foundation/media/store.test.ts:186-200`. (Modules survey NR-1, finding 6.)
- **NR-2, reference-counted style adoption (G2-D8):** a new row of the plan's Shared repairs table. The per-CSS-text, per-root counting that `tp-map` keeps privately (`src/components/map/map.ts:790-809`) moves into `src/foundation/generated-style.ts` beside `GeneratedStyleResource` (`:51`), and `tp-map` and the editor adopt through it the adapter base CSS and the CSS of custom nodes, which the plan's widget `host.ts` would otherwise have adopted with a copy (C-050, C-451, C-560). C-577 and V-836. (Modules survey NR-2.)
- **NR-3, `{name}` template filling (G2-D8):** a new row of the plan's Shared repairs table. One internal foundation module (not `intl.ts`, which `src/foundation/index.ts:25` re-exports) replaces flow's `format` (`src/widgets/flow/strings.ts:151-155`, 21 calls in the 6 flow modules that import it), the copy of File upload (`src/components/file-upload/messages.ts:140-143`) and the inline replacements of the emoji picker (`src/widgets/emoji-picker/emoji-picker.ts:239`, `:924`), and the editor's companion `strings.ts` and announcer use it, since the companion cannot import flow. C-578 and V-837. (Modules survey NR-3.)
- **NR-4, `domError` (G2-D8):** a new row of the plan's Shared repairs table. ### Approved-plan amendments: in-document image upload (2026-10-27)

User decision (2026-10-27): "We need to get rid of the popover. The editor must support image sizes, types, progress and errors." Gates 0–2 for this bounded change:

- **Gate 0, sources:** live Widgets spec 0.45.1 (`8affdfcd`): `uwg-te-req-surfaces-4` (image popover), `-surfaces-2`, `-surfaces-6`, `-content-6`, `-a11y-2`, `-ana-3`, `-prop-1`, `-evt-5`, `-tools-2`, tables `uwg-te-tab-anatomy-r15`, `-props-r13`, `-reasons-r9/r12/r13`, `-vocabulary-r10`; the File upload contract (`docs/file-upload.md`: `accept`, `max-file-size`, `uploader`, `tp-upload-complete`, `tp-upload-error`, `tp-file-reject`, Retry). References: neither reference uploads in place (Tiptap `extension-file-handler` filters `allowedMimeTypes` and leaves insertion to the application; the Lexical playground's dialog is a bare `accept="image/*"` input), so the block flow is a Tweakpad contract (DD-128).
- **Gate 1, capabilities (C-588–C-594):** C-588 the image tool inserts an image block with an empty source (a pending image) at the point of insertion, no popover; C-589 the adapters render a pending image as an empty host with `tp-te-image-pending` and no visible `img`; C-590 the widget overlays one File upload card (`text-editor-image-upload`) over each pending image block, fed with `imageAccept` and `imageMaxFileSize`, uploading through `imageUpload` with progress, error and Retry from the File upload, and sets `src` through `block.set-attrs` when the upload resolves a source that passes the image policy; C-591 pasted and dropped image files are checked against the same type and size limits, rejected ones reported (`text-editor-upload-rejected`) and announced, accepted ones inserted as pending images at the paste or drop point and uploaded in place; C-592 a pending image is omitted by the HTML, Markdown and text outputs and deleting the block cancels its upload; C-593 the image tool is enabled only while `imageUpload` is set (`context.imageUpload`), a run with a value stays allowed; C-594 the card's drop surface follows the editing root in the Tab sequence and Escape in it returns focus to the editing root.
- **Gate 2, owners:** the pending state lives in the model as `src: ''` (no new block kind, no nullable type); the overlay card follows the placeholder layer pattern (`OverlayLayer`, `blockElement`/`blockRects`, transform placement, no engine DOM writes, `uwg-te-req-engine-9`); the card is the library's File upload (type, size, progress, error, Retry, Remove), no local progress or error UI; the policy check stays in the shared block edits; the popover, its lane, its strings and its part are removed (no shims: no-legacy rule). Affected consumers: `views/popups.ts`, `text-editor.ts`, `tools/resolve.ts` (popup semantics), `views/suggestions.ts` (surface entries), `views/lanes.ts`, the fixture lane probe and README, the docs and the Image upload story.

### Approved-plan amendments: opt-in features and per-engine entries (2026-10-27)

User decisions (2026-10-27): split the adapter entry per engine; no lazy loading and no load-time optimization, the optional controls are opt-in by import so a bundler drops what a page does not import; the image and table options live on the feature factories; without features the widget is the core editor; six features; no aliases or compatibility shims.

- **Gate 0, sources:** the measured bundle (0.1.2: `tp-text-editor` 974 kB / 287 kB gzip, of which ~17% widget code, ~30% composed components, ~33% shared foundation; the adapter entry 390 kB / 121 kB gzip with both adapters), the Carousel effects precedent (`effect` property + imported factories, `docs/carousel.md`), `defineElement` recursion (`src/foundation/define.ts`), `adoptStyleText` (`src/foundation/generated-style.ts`), the packaging research (`tmp/component-verification/text-editor/design/research-lib-packaging-precedent.md` §5, option (ii) superseded by the user), `uwg-te-req-pkg-1`.
- **Gate 1, capabilities (C-600–C-608):** C-600 per-engine entries; C-601 the `features` property and the six factories; C-602 the feature contract (`feature.ts`); C-603 element definition on attach and style adoption; C-604 the core element dependencies and styles; C-605 the built-in tool sets per feature and the identifier-only `ids.ts`; C-606 absent-feature layout rule; C-607 duplicate-feature diagnostic; C-608 the size report's all-features row and core assertion. A widget-side Markdown opt-in was ruled out: `format.markdown` is a base capability that both adapters implement through `adapters/shared/content.ts`, so the markdown chain is in every adapter graph.
- **Spec:** committed in Spec Blocks as `cd00e10f` (0.45.2): `uwg-te-req-pkg-1` (adapter sub-entries), `uwg-te-par-def-1`, `uwg-te-par-engine-1`, `uwg-te-req-engine-1`, the props table (`features` row added; `stickyTableHeaders`, `imageUpload`, `imageAccept`, `imageMaxFileSize` rows removed), `uwg-te-req-prop-1`, the new `uwg-te-req-prop-5` (features), `uwg-te-req-surfaces-4`, `uwg-te-req-tables-9`, the anatomy table and the conformance list.
- **Gate 2, owners:** the feature runtimes are the existing view aggregates (`views/blocks.ts`, `views/tables.ts`) and the pieces of the dissolved `views/popups.ts`, built by each feature's `attach` over one `TextEditorFeatureHost` the element builds once; the shared selection anchor moves to `views/selection-anchor.ts`; the Alt+F10 order constants move to `focus.ts` (`TEXT_EDITOR_CONTEXTUAL_ORDER`); feature styles move beside their views and are adopted on attach; the presentation family and recipe stay one dictionary.

### Module table

Paths in the Module column are relative to the group's folder where the group names one; elsewhere paths are written from the repository root, and a bare `:line` repeats the previous path. In the Consumers column, "applications" marks a public export: from `@tweakpad/ui/text-editor` or `@tweakpad/ui/widgets`, or for a shared owner from `@tweakpad/ui` or a subpath. A module that a decision adds without naming its file is given by its folder; its file name is fixed when it lands.

### Shared repairs

Each repair has one owner. Column notes:
- **Regression scenario IDs:** the repair's own rows come first, then the editor-side acceptance rows of other groups in parentheses. V-817–V-832 are the regression rows that gate 2 adds for scenarios the repairs lacked; NR-1 to NR-8 have the capability rows C-576–C-583 and one regression row each, V-835–V-842, in order. NR-9 (R-04) and NR-10 (the deep-freeze owner) were added at the M4 exit with C-584, C-585 and V-848, V-849. NR-11 (the Toolbar's fully disabled mode, X-TB) was added at M6's RW-0 with C-586 and V-853.
- **Lands before:** "Before M6" means the repair is implemented in M5 and lands before the first integration (I-01 to I-03). G2-D9 and G2-D10 as corrected land NR-5 and NR-6 in M5; G2-D8, G2-D11 and G2-D12 give the other NR repairs no milestone, so their column names the milestone of the first editor consumer.
- R4, R7 and R15 include the round-3 plan follow-ups (R3-D11, the AltGraph narrowing, the accent fill).

### Presentation source map

Registry base: a composed region inherits the preset that its library recipe already adopted from the registry checkout `../specification/external/ui/apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/` ("registry" below; `ui/button.tsx`, `toggle`, `toggle-group`, `separator`, `dropdown-menu`, `popover`, `command`, `tooltip`, `kbd`, `input-group`, `field`, `badge`, `table`, `resizable`, `checkbox`, `spinner`) on the library theme; widget-only regions have no upstream presentation (engine UI is not used) and take layout only from the five reference screenshots. The public parts are the 26 of B4b `uwg-te-tab-anatomy` (17), `uwg-te-tab-anatomy-status` (1) and `uwg-te-tab-anatomy-tables` (8); the positioned surface, the underlay, the drag preview and the column-resize guide carry no part (R4-D2). Engine-rendered content is painted through the `tp-te-*` vocabulary (B4b `uwg-te-tab-vocabulary` r1-r17) by descendant rules of the `text-editor-content` part, never by family part bindings, which add the part to every match in the shadow root (`presentation/controller.ts:234-248`; G2-D21). Paths are relative to `src/` unless they start with `tests/`, `docs/` or `../`; `recipes/` is `src/presentation/recipes/`; lines checked on `5afca9c` (2026-10-16).

### Implementation and composition reuse map

Every nested UI role in the widget's internals, its docs, stories and examples and its fixtures names the library component, or the native anatomy with the reason it is no substitute (B4b `uwg-te-req-ana-1`, C-420); the tag census V-560, which gains `tp-badge` (G2-D26), checks the rendered result. A missing capability names the shared repair that supplies it (R1–R26, NR-1–NR-8) and, where one is allocated, its regression scenario. Paths as in the presentation source map.
